monthly_review.summary: You've reduced volume and shifted effort toward higher-intensity zones this month, resulting in faster average pace and elevated HR—but at the cost of aerobic TE and efficiency. Your training is becoming more race-specific but may be under-fueling base endurance.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 4 time jumped from 3% to 21% of total HR distribution—nearly a 7x increase—while Zone 1+2 dropped from 79% to 52%, signaling a sharp shift away from easy aerobic development.

goal_tracker.message: You need 22.3 more km across 5 remaining sessions (avg 4.5 km/session) to match last month’s 46.0 km — achievable with one longer run (8–10 km) and four moderate runs (3.5–4.5 km each).

insights.title: Efficiency declined despite cadence gain
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.42 to 13.19 km/hr per bpm while cadence rose from 146 to 150 spm — suggesting improved neuromuscular coordination isn’t yet translating to metabolic economy, likely due to increased Z3/Z4 time (45% this month vs 22% last month) reducing time spent in truly efficient, fat-burning zones.

insights.title: Overreliance on Zone 4 with minimal Zone 5 stimulus
insights.body: Zone 4 now comprises 21% of HR time (up from 3%), yet Zone 5 remains only 3% — indicating frequent threshold efforts without sufficient VO2 max or neuromuscular speed work. This risks plateauing at lactate threshold without raising ceiling.

insights.title: Stride length variability reflects inconsistent pacing
insights.body: Stride length ranged from 68.8 cm (slow 0.5 km @ 9:50/km) to 94.7 cm (fast 1.0 km @ 7:03/km), a 37% swing — consistent with the recent 3-run day where pace varied by 2:27/km. Ground contact time stayed stable (310–330 ms), suggesting form integrity is maintained but pacing discipline needs refinement.

insights.title: Aerobic TE dropped despite higher avg HR
insights.body: Avg HR rose +8 bpm (136 → 144) while avg aerobic TE fell from 2.7 to 2.4 — confirming that added intensity did not yield commensurate aerobic stimulus; instead, it appears to be displacing lower-HR, higher-TE easy running essential for capillary and mitochondrial development.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a pure Zone 2 session: 6 km at 130–135 bpm (per Garmin Z2 range), maintaining pace ≤550 sec/km (9:10/km), cadence ≥146 spm.
recommendations.reason: Last month’s Z1+Z2 share was 79% (ideal for aerobic base); this month it’s only 52%. Re-establishing low-HR volume will restore aerobic TE and efficiency.

recommendations.action: Replace one upcoming run with a 6 × 90-sec stride drill: 90 sec @ ~422 sec/km (7:02/km) followed by 90 sec walk/jog recovery, focusing on landing midfoot and holding cadence ≥160 spm.
recommendations.reason: Your best pace is 422 sec/km but only appears once in recent data — and vertical oscillation spikes to 9.2 cm during fast efforts, suggesting inefficiency at speed. Strides improve neuromuscular coordination without taxing HR.

recommendations.action: Add 2 min of post-run mobility: 1 min single-leg calf raises (20 reps/leg) + 1 min banded glute bridges (30 sec/leg), starting after your June 10 run.
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time is consistently 310–314 ms in longer runs — solid — but vertical oscillation increased to 9.2 cm during your fastest recent effort (June 4), indicating possible glute/calf fatigue or stiffness limiting elastic return.

weekly_focus.description: Rebuild fat-burning capacity and HR discipline through intentional low-zone volume, while introducing controlled neuromuscular priming to support future speed gains — all without increasing weekly run count beyond 4–5.
suggested_sessions: Recovery walk or cross-train + mobility routine
